extraction.document_summary: Great Eastern “Prestige Legacy Index” is a Singapore life insurance plan that combines lifetime protection with index-linked wealth-building via Index Account(s). The document states protection is “up to 13 times2 the premium paid” and that investment returns are based on selected global indices with “a guaranteed minimum floor rate of 0% p.a.” It highlights a “guaranteed crediting rate of 4.20% p.a. for the first year,” then thereafter uses a prevailing rate “with a guaranteed minimum crediting rate of 2.00% p.a.” depending on index performance, caps and participation. For flexible premiums, it references “loyalty crediting rate” awarded under conditions, and a terminal illness/death benefit paid when death or terminal illness occurs before/after the policy anniversary after the 121st birthday. A key caveat is that “All figures are illustrated” and results depend on index performance and product terms in the policy contract.
quality_notes: Several sections appear truncated/garbled (e.g., “choose from 4 premium” and participation/percentage figures are not readable in full).
No explicit underwriting, entry age range, free-look/grace period, surrender/cash value, or limit amounts are stated in clear text.
The death/terminal illness benefit trigger is partially stated (timing vs 121st birthday anniversary), but exact payout formula/amount is not provided.

policies.quick_summary: Index-linked Great Eastern life insurance with Index Account(s) credited by global index performance (0% floor), including a guaranteed 4.20% crediting rate in year 1 and 2.00% guaranteed minimum thereafter. Lifetime protection includes a Death or Terminal Illness Benefit, with payment logic tied to whether death/terminal illness occurs before or after the policy anniversary after age 121. Premiums can be single premium or flexible premiums (5 or 10 years planned). Key limitations include illustration-only figures and index-credited mechanics subject to participation/caps and product terms in the policy contract.
